assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric and topological phases changed how quantum mechanics is understood: gauge potentials have physical consequences in field-free regions, and adiabatic evolution carries a gauge-invariant phase. The ideas now underlie polarization, Hall conductance, topological band theory and molecular conical intersections. Berry's phase also sits close to quantum chaos and semiclassics, which I know well. Originality and clarity are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov-Bohm (1959) and Berry (1984) are distinct discoveries, so a joint prize would honour a conceptual lineage rather than one result. Aharonov and Berry fit the two-name configuration. Bohm is deceased and Ehrenberg and Siday made earlier related contributions, which makes the historical credit imperfect. Pancharatnam's earlier work is also part of the Berry-phase history.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades, in electron interferometry, neutron and optical experiments and in molecular systems. The interpretation is stable. If anything the recognition is overdue, and the timing risk is that the topic may seem too foundational or old-fashioned.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase as one coherent discovery or two.
Priority claims by Ehrenberg-Siday and Pancharatnam are not something I can verify independently here.
Whether the prize is better aimed at the downstream topological-matter consequences.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermittency and anomalous scaling in fully developed turbulence are among the central unsolved problems of classical statistical physics. Multifractal descriptions and experimental measurement of structure-function exponents shaped the field and linked it to dynamical systems and critical phenomena. This is close to my own work on particles in turbulent flows, so I weigh the importance of a quantitative statistical theory heavily. Clarity is limited, since no first-principles derivation of the exponents exists.
assessment.attribution: Frisch (multifractal and beta models, with Parisi and others) and Sreenivasan (experimental scaling, universality) are the natural pair. Parisi has already been recognized in 2021 for different work, and Kolmogorov, Kraichnan and Mandelbrot are deceased or peripheral. Credit for the multifractal formalism is spread over several theorists beyond those two names. The pairing of theory and experiment is reasonable.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena are very well established experimentally and numerically, but the theoretical explanation remains incomplete. This is a maturity concern: the prize would recognize a framework and measurements rather than a closed theory.
uncertainties: Whether the theory is a settled discovery or an incomplete framework.
Credit is diffuse across several theorists, including Parisi, whose prize was for other work.
I may be biased toward turbulence by my own research field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened a new, tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. The field of moire quantum matter has grown very quickly, with clear conceptual originality and a close link between theory and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction (2011), and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery with Cao and others. This fits three names but leaves out Cao as first author and other contributors, including Dean, Young and Ashoori for related moire work. Credit for the many later moire systems is not resolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups within a few years, but the mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states are still debated. Recognition may be somewhat early, though impact is already very high.
uncertainties: Superconducting mechanism is unresolved.
Boundaries of credit among moire-materials contributors, including graduate student authorship.
Possible timing prematurity relative to older mature candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unifies granular matter, foams, emulsions and glasses by a rigidity transition with critical scaling, isostaticity and anomalous vibrational modes. It is a conceptual statistical-physics framework for disordered matter, with a clear originality and wide reach into soft matter and also into optimization and learning landscapes.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel authored the 1998 jamming phase diagram proposal and subsequent work, and O'Hern, Silbert and Langer contributed the numerical establishment of point J. Two names are a defensible configuration, though the 2003 numerical work shares credit.
assessment.maturity: Simulations and experiments confirm much of the scaling, but the relation to the glass transition and the status of the critical-point analogy remain contested. Mature in age, less so in a settled theory.
uncertainties: Whether jamming is a true critical point with universal exponents.
Credit shared with O'Hern, Silbert, Langer and others.
Distance of the framework from a single decisive experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at 10^-18 precision underlie a redefinition of the second, tests of relativity and variation of constants, relativistic geodesy and possible dark-matter searches. The magic-wavelength idea by Katori and the many-body clock engineering by Ye are original and measurably decisive. This is a clear case of an invention with lasting scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept, and Ye's group made the leading precision and many-body demonstrations. Hall and Hansch were already recognized in 2005 for the comb. Two laureates is a clean configuration, with credit for ion clocks (Wineland, Rosenband) falling in a different, already partly recognized branch.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several laboratories with consistent results. The technology is mature enough for recognition, though the redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 recognition and with ion-clock contributions.
Whether the prize is wanted before the redefinition of the SI second.
Possible competing credit for other lattice-clock groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their proposals for trapped-ion quantum gates (1995) and for ultracold-atom quantum simulation provided the blueprint for experimental quantum information processors and simulators. The theoretical clarity and the realized experiments make the impact large.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the identifiable theorists behind both proposals. The set is a compact two-person configuration. Credit overlaps with Wineland and Monroe on the experimental side, and the 2012 prize already recognized some of this work.
assessment.maturity: Many experiments have realized the proposals, and trapped-ion platforms are continuing to mature. Recognition seems timely, but the field is evolving fast.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with 2022 quantum-information recognition.
Whether theory credit can be separated from the experimental platforms.
Whether quantum computing is considered sufficiently mature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new classification of band insulators, linking Z2 invariants, protected edge states and spin-orbit physics. The theory was original and the experimental realization in HgTe wells was decisive.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall effect. Molenkamp led the experiment in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. That leaves out Zhang, who is deceased, and Bernevig and Hughes, so the trio does not map neatly onto the decisive contributions. Moore, Balents and Fu-Kane for 3D are further complications.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation including ARPES of 3D topological insulators is strong, and the concept is widely adopted. The 2016 prize already covered topological phases partially, which affects timing.
uncertainties: Credit among Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Kane, Mele and Molenkamp.
Overlap with the 2016 Nobel Prize topic.
Practical consequences are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong single-photon coupling controllable on a chip and became the architecture of superconducting qubits, readout and quantum processors. The conceptual step is clear and the technological reach large.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf are named, while the experimental demonstration in 2004 came from the Yale group including Wallraff, who is not in the supplied credited names. This limits a fair configuration, and the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits touches adjacent ground.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many laboratories and now an industrial platform. Highly mature, though the allocation of credit among theory and experiment is unsettled.
uncertainties: Wallraff is not available as a credited name.
Overlap with the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.
Boundary between this and quantum-computing hardware credit.
